At each currently own position, require a data descriptor and compare its value with the last retained observation there using SameValue. An own accessor descriptor throws a TypeError exception at this phase, even when its observed value satisfied the element type. A discrepancy throws a TypeError exception. A missing own position on a non-extensible Array also throws a TypeError exception at this phase. These inspections use internal own descriptors and do not invoke getters.

    Perform required materializations, value copies, and ordinary writes in the retained order already specified. Track their resulting values for initialization. Recheck the Array's length before and after each affected materialization and write. An outer write must recheck length, own presence, and an own data value captured immediately before that write at its own definition, after lookup and conversion effects. A discrepancy throws a TypeError exception. Scope this check to the receiver, key, and executing outer write; callback and nested operations remain independent. Remove the scope on normal or abrupt completion. Earlier abrupt completions retain precedence.

    After all required ordinary writes succeed, validate every new Array initialization plan before publishing any still-missing positions or new contracts. The length must still match. An originally own position must still be own. A still-missing position must permit an own definition. Every current own position must have a data descriptor, including when backing was independently established during ordinary effects. Unless backing was independently established, its data value must be SameValue to its prepared value. A discrepancy throws a TypeError exception. Preserve independently established backing, including its completed effects, and validate its length and own presence without replacing its contract. These checks do not reread elements or replace own accessors with data. The judgment concerns current descriptors: independently replacing an accessor with matching data can satisfy it; installing an accessor after preflight cannot. A representation refusal after a union alternative was selected does not retry another alternative.

    After all plans validate, create each still-missing own element as a writable, enumerable, configurable data property holding its prepared value, and publish the admission's new backing contracts. There is no user-code execution between this validation, initialization, and publication. These definitions neither call inherited setters nor repeat getters, conversions, or defaults. Existing own descriptors, including a matching data property created by an ordinary materialization write, retain their attributes. A failure publishes none of the admission's still-pending initialization or new contracts; earlier ordinary writes, independent definitions, and nested boundaries survive. Filling positions within the admitted extent does not itself grow, remove, or relocate storage or establish a new reference invalidation event. Retained observations are current-state checks, not a lease against user-code mutation.

    The retained-admission requirements also apply to tuple elements. Retain the element values and admitted union contracts of the assignment selected by SequenceAssignment, not evidence belonging only to an unsuccessful candidate. For required fixed positions and at most one unbounded homogeneous array rest, retain the complete prefix, rest and suffix domains. At an admitted length n, a suffix of s required positions starts at index n - s; positions between the prefix and suffix have the rest element type. The minimum length is the sum of the required prefix and suffix widths. This assignment follows from the length, including when the rest is empty, and is not selected from current element values. Acquire these complete domains, after required materializations, value copies and ordinary writes succeed. Preserve existing backing contracts and use the same failure and publication rules as for homogeneous-array admission. A later compatible view does not store the elements again.

    For a tuple without a rest, trailing defaults do not suppress retained admission of supplied positions. Retain each supplied value and selected callable contract on the same terms as a required position, including when the tuple is reached through another structural contract. Its complete storage domain includes every integer length from its required prefix width through its total position count, with each existing index governed by that declared position's type. Acquiring this domain or constructing a fully default-filled tuple does not freeze it at the observed or maximum length. Existing backing remains authoritative. Membership and viability do not fill omitted positions; conversion that fills an omitted trailing default retains the construction rules of 1.4.2.7. A supplied hole or supplied undefined is not an omitted position.

    A converting boundary receiving a no-rest tuple with omitted trailing positions must complete those positions even when membership of an enclosing structural contract or selected union member succeeds. Retain a construction obligation with the observed source, supplied values, resolved tuple type, selected subvalue evidence, and already formed defaults. An independent membership or viability judgment retains no such obligation. A fully supplied compatible tuple continues to use in-place admission. An omitted position is determined by the observed length, not by a supplied hole or undefined.

    For each selected construction, create a separate Array using the receiving realm's Array prototype, its retained supplied values, and the declared values of its omitted defaults. Do not reread source properties, rerun a default initializer, grow the source, acquire replacement backing on the source, or copy an enclosing container merely to fill this tuple. A source accessor may supply a retained value for this genuine copy, and a non-extensible source does not itself prevent the copy. Newly owned output elements remain own data locations. Apply required callable materialization, nested construction, and value copying to the output, and acquire its complete tuple storage domain before the result can escape through an enclosing ordinary Set. The source's existing backing and reference locations remain authoritative.

    Where retained paths reach the same receiving Object, property key and observed value, and any of them requires this construction, carry all of their retained subvalue evidence into that construction, including a path that does not itself fill defaults. Their observed supplied lengths and required completed lengths must agree, and the declared defaults at every omitted position must be SameValue. The completed length must satisfy every retained tuple and homogeneous-array length domain. Reject an incompatible plan with a TypeError exception during the surrounding admission's combined-plan validation, before its materialization writes. Do not choose one path's defaults by traversal order or memoize a result solely by source identity across different receiving locations. The ordinary equal-consecutive-observation rule continues to govern shared materializations and writes.

    Complete the selected construction using all its retained positional and homogeneous contracts. A newly appended value must satisfy their combined position contract; a declared default validated at type formation does not by itself establish a different retained obligation. Retained object contracts apply to the produced Array rather than to custom properties of the source: a required property unavailable on that Array throws a TypeError exception; an absent optional property contributes no acquisition; a newly present declared property or a newly produced key governed by an index signature must satisfy its contract. Reuse retained evidence for unchanged supplied values, and check changed or newly produced values without rereading the source. Do not acquire contracts solely for optional source properties absent from the output.

    At the reached nested construction boundary, finish the output's required checks, materializations, copies, own-data initialization and backing publication before the enclosing ordinary Set. Keep the enclosing admission's earlier preflight and retained write order. A false Set result throws a TypeError exception and an abrupt result propagates; neither resumes selection at another union member. A later enclosing failure publishes none of that enclosing admission's pending contracts, but does not roll back an earlier write or a nested output whose boundary completed before it was passed to a setter. Separate nested boundaries do not form a transaction over the reachable alias graph. Allocating a separate tuple does not remove or relocate the source's locations. A reference to an enclosing receiving property observes its ordinary replacement under the existing reference rules.

    A proof used to elide a receiving boundary must also establish that no omitted tuple construction or other retained materialization remains. The backing type's permitted length interval alone does not establish current occupancy, including for a previously typed enclosing object whose nested tuple was shortened. Such a proof may use internal facts without introducing observable reads; otherwise preserve the required boundary. These rules do not change default evaluation at type formation, its evaluable-fragment limits, later storage growth through DefaultValueOf, or the separate assignment requirements for tuples containing rests.

    Intersect a defaulted tuple's complete length interval and positional types with all other contracts acquired in the same admission. A finite maximum is not by itself a fixed extent; flatten the combined domain to one length only if that is its sole permitted length. Later shortening, growth and intrinsic mutation use the existing tuple-domain and surviving-location checks. An unsupplied newly exposed position uses DefaultValueOf of its actual backing type under the initialization rules, not the tuple's construction initializer. Removal invalidates the removed location's references, and later regrowth does not revive them. A defaulted position does not authorize a hole.

    When one admission acquires several such tuple or homogeneous-array contracts on the same previously untyped Array, intersect their complete length domains and their types at every permitted position. A fixed extent bounds the complete domain; required prefixes and suffixes contribute their combined minimum length. Keep every suffix aligned to the end at each permitted length rather than flattening it at the initially observed length. An empty intersection of length domains throws a TypeError exception before element materialization. Do not select only the first or last path's contract or record only currently occupied indices. A contract independently established during an ordinary write is preserved.

    For these required prefix/rest/suffix contracts, a length change must preserve SameType between the old and proposed backing types at every index below both lengths, as well as remaining in the permitted length domain. This judgment does not depend on whether a reference is currently live. An indexed store or definition that grows the Array applies this judgment before element conversion and obtains its destination contract at the proposed length. A length assignment applies it before removing elements. A failure throws a TypeError exception. It neither removes a surviving location nor establishes a new reference invalidation event. Existing value initialization, descriptor, write and liveness obligations still apply; preserving contracts alone does not establish initialized values in newly exposed positions.

    At a statically known length, contextual typing of a literal against such a tuple uses this same exact assignment. Where existing static index analysis establishes a positional read at index i without a known length, its read domain is the union of the types that can occupy that index over permitted lengths. A required prefix position is exact. Beyond a prefix of width p, this includes the rest type and suffix entries zero through min(i - p, s - 1), where s is the suffix width. This read union is not a writable backing contract and does not widen an invariant reference. A statically expanded fixed spread can establish a literal length; an unresolved spread cannot.

    A successful sequence assignment is evidence for that admission, not permission to replace an existing location's declared contract. Later stores, including stores through invariant references, continue to check the backing location type. A new assignment selected from current values does not by itself relocate or remove storage and therefore does not invalidate existing references under 2.10. These admission requirements do not change the restrictions on moving values between differently typed tuple positions in 1.14.10.

    Eliding a boundary must preserve required storage-contract acquisition. A proof that the current value satisfies a structural type does not alone prove that the backing contract exists. Acquisition can be omitted only where its result is already established, or retained separately from an elided check without introducing new observable evaluation. Discarding speculative admission evidence does not roll back the ordinary effects of a conversion or a nested boundary that completed before a later failure. These rules establish no reference-liveness permission.

    Owned typed Array elements are own data locations, including elements whose declared type is any and tuple positions. An indexed accessor descriptor cannot be installed in that backing. After ordinary property-key and descriptor conversion, retain the existing fixed-extent and tuple-domain judgments and the earlier ordinary nonwritable-length refusal for growth. At the reached indexed storage check, an accessor descriptor throws a TypeError exception, whether the element exists, whether its current descriptor is configurable, and whether the operation was called through Object.defineProperty or Reflect.defineProperty. This refusal leaves the current descriptor, value, length, capacity and location identity unchanged. Ordinary generic/data descriptor updates and non-index properties retain their existing rules; Object.defineProperties retains earlier completed definitions before a later refusal. Independently acquired object-property contracts still constrain definitions, including on otherwise untyped Arrays, and their abrupt completions are propagated.

    The own-data requirement adds no per-read accessor conversion and does not silently materialize an own getter into storage. Independent membership can observe accessor values without acquiring backing. Inherited values used to initialize missing own data retain the admission rules above. A genuine elementwise copy creates separate data storage and leaves source accessors unchanged; a compatible cast that retains identity still performs owned-storage admission. The general property-reference eligibility rule does not authorize a descriptor prohibited by the receiver's backing contract. Ordinary accessor properties and non-index Array properties remain borrowable through ordinary Get and Set. A failed accessor replacement does not itself invalidate a reference; independently completed removal or relocation retains its own liveness effects.

    A store to a typed field or a typed element checks the value against the field's or element's declared type, by Table 23. Deleting a typed field, a typed element, or a member required by an implemented interface is a type error. Where the receiver type and property key statically establish that the deletion targets such storage, the source is rejected before evaluation under 1.2.8. Otherwise the attempted deletion throws a TypeError exception.

    For a union receiver, this storage judgment is established when every reachable alternative on which the deletion executes establishes prohibited storage at the selected key. An optional chain's short-circuited alternatives perform no deletion. A genuinely unresolved alternative does not establish this judgment. The predicate is about deletion, not whether an element read would be in bounds: an ordinary absent property or a key beyond every fixed extent is not made a protected position by the union. The same single-receiver storage judgment, including the protected index domains below, is applied independently to each executing alternative.

    The deletion proof also ranges over a statically established finite set of property keys, using String values and actual Symbol identities. It is a type error when every executing receiver/key alternative establishes protected storage. An unknown key or receiver, or a legal fixed-container nonposition, defeats this all-invalid proof. Do not apply the bounds judgment for a read to the operand of delete.

    For example, delete _a_[0] is rejected before evaluation when a has type [2].<uint8> or [uint8], even inside a function that is never called. This is a judgment about deletion, not the bounds of an element read: a key beyond a fixed tuple's positions and an ordinary property not declared by the type are not typed positions. A receiver or key whose type does not settle the judgment retains the runtime check. The prohibition on deleting typed storage does not change the rules for resizing an array or for the liveness of references into it.

    The statically protected index domain includes each canonical array index of a growable homogeneous typed array, every written fixed tuple position including one with a default, and the tail of a tuple with a proved trailing unbounded array rest. Current occupancy is not queried: deletion at such an index is a type error even when a growable array or its trailing rest is currently empty. A fixed, nested or non-final rest does not by itself prove an unbounded domain; unresolved domains and keys retain runtime checking. Noncanonical string properties and fixed tuple nonpositions remain outside this domain. Union and optional-deletion rules continue to combine the executing alternatives, and neither resizing nor reference liveness changes.

    A class whose fields are typed may opt out with the dynamic modifier, which leaves it unsealed. Such a class cannot be used for sequential data and cannot be a value type in a typed array.

    Note 2

    Sealing is what makes a typed field's type a fact about the layout rather than a claim about the initializer. Without it a typed class would be a class whose fields happen to have been assigned values of the right type so far, which is not something an engine can lay out contiguously or an offset can be computed from. The memory layout extension depends on this, and it is the reason sealing is automatic rather than requested: a field's type and a reallocatable object are not compatible, so the type implies the seal.

    1.7.7 The instanceof Operator

    A Type Object has a %Symbol.hasInstance% method. When called with argument v, it returns ? IsOfType(v, the Type Object's [[TypeRecord]]).

    Note

    instanceof therefore extends to every type of this proposal through the protocol the language already has, and needs no new operator. a instanceof uint8 is true for a uint8 binding and a instanceof uint16 is false, a fixed-length array is NOT an instance of the corresponding dynamic-length array type — the extents must agree (1.4.2.7), and Span.<T> is the type that accepts either — and a class is unaffected, since a class's type object is its constructor and the prototype chain semantics apply as they do today. A GENERIC class's specializations are distinct class objects whose prototype chains do not pass through the declaration's prototype, so for x instanceof C where C is the constructor of a generic class declaration, OrdinaryHasInstance is extended: where the ordinary walk returns false, the result is true if some object on x's prototype chain is the prototype of a specialization of that declaration. The declaration is the family: new Box.<uint8>(1) instanceof Box, new Box(1) instanceof Box, and new S(1) instanceof Box for a class S extends Box.<uint8> are true, while instanceof Box.<uint8> is the ordinary walk against that specialization's prototype. A successful check narrows the static type in the branch it guards, which 1.8.5 specifies.

    1.7.8 Typed catch Clauses

    A catch clause may name the type it handles, and a try may then carry more than one. The productions below restate their ECMAScript definitions (1.1).

    TryStatement[Yield, Await, Return] : try Block[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] Catch[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] try Block[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] CatchClauses[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] try Block[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] Finally[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] try Block[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] Catch[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] Finally[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] try Block[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] CatchClauses[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] Finally[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] CatchClauses[Yield, Await, Return] : Catch[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] CatchClauses[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] Catch[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] Catch[Yield, Await, Return] : catch ( CatchParameter[?Yield, ?Await] TypeAnnotation[?Yield, ?Await]opt ) Block[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return] catch Block[?Yield, ?Await, ?Return]

    It is a type error if a Catch other than the last of its CatchClauses has no TypeAnnotation. When a value v is thrown, the clauses are tried in order, and the first runs for which IsOfType(v, its declared type) is true; a Catch with no annotation satisfies every value. The test is membership and not RequireType (1.7.3.1), since a clause binds the thrown value itself and does not convert it: accepting a Number at a numeric type or any value at string by conversion would bind a value that is not of the declared type. It is a type error if a Catch can never run: where it follows a Catch whose annotation denotes any, or where its declared type is a subtype of the union of the declared types of the Catch clauses before it, since IsOfType holds of a value at every supertype of a type it holds at, so an earlier clause accepts every value this one would. This is the rule that an untyped Catch must be last, extended to the typed clauses it has the same reason for. The annotation remains the catch binding's declared store type. On entry, narrow its incoming value by removing the stable members excluded by the failure of all preceding filters, using NarrowFrom and the membership-stability rules of 1.8.5. For example, after catch (e: uint8), a later catch (e: uint8 | string) starts with e narrowed to string; assignment is still checked against uint8 | string and can invalidate that fact. An observable structural membership test supplies no unsupported subtraction proof. This rule does not infer the set of values thrown by the try body. A value no clause accepts propagates as if the try had no catch: typed clauses filter, they do not swallow, so the completion is rethrown after Finally, when present, runs as it does today.

    A destructuring CatchParameter is checked as a binding pattern in the clause's own lexical scope. Its declared filter, where known, supplies the source Static Type for the pattern's contributions and typed bindings. Without a known filter the source is unknown. Independently written member annotations, defaults, rest annotations and pattern source-eligibility judgments apply even when the handler or default is never selected. This judgment does not infer the set of values thrown by the try body and does not convert the filtered value. Ordered dispatch, property and iterator effects, reference decay and liveness are unchanged.

    Note

    This is the design's error handling document made normative: ordered dispatch, first match, an untyped tail for the rest. A rejected promise reaches a typed clause through await unchanged, since await rethrows the rejection reason and the dispatch above neither knows nor cares that the throw crossed an async boundary. The errors this proposal itself raises, RangeError at a checked numeric conversion and at an out-of-bounds access, TypeError at a dynamic boundary, are ordinary values here, so catch (e: RangeError) handles every range failure in one clause (design, errorhandling.md).

    1.8 Declarations

    This clause gives meaning to the annotations the grammar attached to bindings in 1.4.4. It specifies what a typed binding holds before it is assigned, what a typed initializer infers, what an assignment to a typed binding does, the declaration that names a type, and the narrowing by which a test refines the type of a binding in the branch it guards.

    1.8.1 Type Alias Declarations

    A type alias declaration names a type. It is added to the declaration forms.

    Declaration[Yield, Await] : HoistableDeclaration[?Yield, ?Await, ~Default] ClassDeclaration[?Yield, ?Await, ~Default] LexicalDeclaration[+In, ?Yield, ?Await] TypeAliasDeclaration[?Yield, ?Await] TypeAliasDeclaration[Yield, Await] : type [no LineTerminator here] BindingIdentifier[?Yield, ?Await] TypeParameters[?Yield, ?Await]opt = Type[?Yield, ?Await] WhereClauses[?Yield, ?Await]opt ;

    A type alias declaration with no TypeParameters creates an immutable binding for its BindingIdentifier, initialized to GetTypeObject of the Type Record its Type denotes. The name is therefore usable in expression position, where it evaluates to that Type Object, and in type position, where it denotes the type. A declaration with TypeParameters creates no binding and is usable only in type position, since a generic alias denotes a type for each list of arguments rather than one type.

    A completed alias result retained from an initialized binding is evidence only for that binding. Resolve a later reference in its source environment, following an indirect import to its target binding. Neither an alias in an unrelated scope nor another evaluation of the same declaration supplies that result merely because its name or source declaration is equal. A nearer binding, including one that is uninitialized or is not an alias, prevents falling back to an outer alias's completed result. If checking has selected a source declaration, a retained result from a different declaration cannot replace it. These requirements apply across successive Scripts in one Realm as well as within a Script or Module.

    Publish such binding evidence only after the alias's initialization succeeds. A computation that has not initialized that binding, including a failed or incomplete declaration preparation, supplies no evidence that the binding contains a completed alias. The temporary recursive record used while forming an alias is distinct from this evidence and does not make an unrelated read initialized. This rule does not prevent checking an available alias definition by its source declaration under the existing declaration-preparation rules. Retained results remain subject to 1.6.2.7; neither publication nor successful type resolution proves reference liveness or permits an otherwise invalid read.

    When checking retains a type obligation for later evaluation, retain the lexical declarations and determining inputs of that obligation and of each producer it calls or reads. Reconstruct a helper's environment from the declarations visible at the helper's source, including transitive helper and alias dependencies; the consumer's same-named bindings do not replace those captures. A retained constant input belongs to its producing binding, not to every reference with that spelling. Form an available alias definition in its own declaration environment, preserving its ordinary recursive and refinement semantics. This formation supplies a checking result without initializing or publishing an unrelated program binding.

    A generic alias dependency retains the environment of its declaration and the captured generic bindings on which its expansion depends. Resolve written type arguments at their use site. Bind omitted defaults and check parameter constraints in the alias's declaration environment, with preceding parameter bindings available in declaration order, and evaluate the selected alias definition in that environment with the resulting bindings. A same-named binding or generic parameter of the consumer does not replace a capture. An available closed generic alias application is not left unresolved solely because the dependency is generic; apply its result to the retained checking obligation. An application requiring an unavailable runtime input remains subject to the existing deferral rule.

    Any internal representation of an unapplied generic alias must distinguish declaration contexts with different determining inputs, including different activations of a captured binding. This does not create an ordinary binding for the generic alias and does not add nominal identity to the expanded type. Reuse of an expansion remains subject to 1.6.2.7. Restore temporary declaration environments and generic parameter bindings after expansion, including abrupt completion, deferral and budget exhaustion; successful expansion supplies no initialization or reference-liveness permission.

    A selected source binding whose required runtime inputs are unavailable remains unresolved under its existing deferral rule. It must not fall through to an older or outer binding with the same name, and executing an ordinary enclosing body is not a way to manufacture the input. A missing reference does not acquire a declaration from the consumer's scope. Imported inputs retain their actual target bindings and the availability and failure rules of 1.3.8. Preserve these requirements for ordinary deferred annotations, computed result obligations, trial specialization, successive Scripts and dynamically constructed function sources. A temporary checking environment and its completed results supply no initialization or reference-liveness permission.

    Note 1

    A Type Object may escape through an ordinary return, stored value or export. Its value and ordinary type identity remain available through that value; the alias's local name does not thereby enter another scope. Implementations may retain declaration provenance beside an environment binding or recover equivalent evidence from a binding's Type Object. No realm-wide name registry, particular cache representation, additional property on a user object or retention of a dead environment is required.

     Note 2

    type Point = { x: float32, y: float32 }; is therefore close to a const whose value is a type object, and the two spellings agree: Point === type { x: float32, y: float32 } is true, because Type Objects are interned (1.2.2.9). What the declaration adds over the const is that the name is also usable where a type is expected. An alias is transparent: it introduces no new type, so Point and its expansion are the same type and are mutually assignable, and a nominal type is created only by a class, an interface, or an enum.

    An alias may refer to itself, directly or through other aliases, provided every cycle passes through a position that holds a reference rather than an inline layout: a member written T | null, the element of a dynamic array, or a field of a sealed class. It is a type error if a cycle never does, since the type would demand an infinite inline layout, which is the same rule 1.11.2 applies to a value type class containing itself. The fixpoint of 1.2.7.3 validates a computed cycle by this rule.

    Note 3

    An OPTIONAL member does not break a cycle. { next?: L } demands the inline layout { next: L } does, because a member that may be ABSENT still needs room for the value where it is present; T | null breaks one because a null member is a reference position, and the size of a reference does not depend on its target's. The two are close in what they admit and far apart in what they cost, which is why they are distinct types (1.4.2.9) even though a read of either yields the union with undefined. A recursive type therefore writes { next: L | null } rather than { next?: L }, and the second is a type error naming the field it reaches itself through.

    The [no LineTerminator here] restriction is what keeps type a contextual keyword. type followed by a line terminator and then an identifier is two statements today, an expression statement naming type and another naming the identifier, and it continues to be. This is the same device the design relies on throughout, and it is why type X = 1; on one line is unambiguous: it is a syntax error today.

    Whether a generic alias may be exported, and how export type Point = ... interacts with the module's binding namespace, is left to the modules clause. A generic alias creating no binding is a decision worth revisiting: it means Grown in type Grown<T: type> = [...Row, T]; cannot be reflected on, while a non-generic alias can be.

    1.8.2 Typed Bindings

    var, let, and const accept the same annotations. A binding declared with a TypeAnnotation has the annotated type; a binding declared without one has the any type. The type of a binding is fixed at its declaration and does not change with what is assigned to it.

    A binding declared with a type and an Initializer is initialized to the value of the initializer, checked against the declared type by the rules of 1.6: the check is static where the initializer's type is known, and is RequireType where the initializer has the any type. A binding declared with a type and no Initializer is initialized to the default value of that type (1.8.3) rather than to undefined.

    A const declaration without an Initializer is a Syntax Error where the binding carries no TypeAnnotation, as it is in ECMA-262: the Early Errors of LexicalDeclaration are amended so that the rule "it is a Syntax Error if Initializer is not present and IsConstantDeclaration of the LexicalDeclaration containing this production is true" does not apply to a LexicalBinding whose BindingIdentifier carries one. Such a binding is initialized to the default value of its type, exactly as a let binding of that type is, and it is a type error where that type has no default (1.8.3.1).

    Note 1

    The annotation is what makes the initializer redundant rather than absent. const c: [].<uint8>; has already said what c holds — a uint8 array, and therefore an empty one — so requiring the program to write = [] as well asks it to repeat the annotation in a second spelling. Every other typed binding takes its type's default; a const that could not would be the one place where an annotation stops carrying that meaning.

    What const promises is unchanged, because it is a promise about the BINDING: the binding does not rebind, and assigning to it remains a TypeError. It has never been a promise that the value is frozen — const a = []; admits a.push(1) — so a defaulted const holding a mutable aggregate is the case that already exists, reached by a different route. The temporal dead zone is likewise unchanged: the default applies at the declaration and not before it, so a read above the declaration is still a ReferenceError.

    A ref binding is a separate rule and keeps its Initializer requirement (2.5): a ref aliases the storage its initializer names, and a type's default is a value rather than a location, so there is nothing for it to alias.

    Assignment to a binding of declared type t checks the assigned value against t by the same rules. The temporal dead zone is unchanged: a let or const binding is uninitialized until its declaration is evaluated, and accessing it before then is a ReferenceError. The default value applies at the declaration, not before it.

    Note 2

    That a typed binding takes its type's default rather than undefined is the point at which a type stops being a claim about a program and becomes a fact about storage. let a: uint32; holds a uint32, so every read of it yields a uint32 and the engine may lay it out as four bytes; were it undefined until assigned, its type would be uint32 | undefined in all but name, and the layout would have to carry a bit saying which. This is the same reason a typed field takes its type's default, and the two rules are one rule.

    1.8.3 Default Values

    1.8.3.1 DefaultValueOf ( t )

    The abstract operation DefaultValueOf takes argument t (a Type Record) and returns either a value of the type t or none. It returns the value a binding or field of the type t holds before it is assigned, or none if t has no default. It performs the following steps when called:

    1. If t.[[Kind]] is nominal and t.[[Declaration]] has a declared zero, then
      1. Let z be the declared zero of t.[[Declaration]].
      2. Return a copy of z.
    2. If t.[[Kind]] is any, return undefined.
    3. If t is a numeric type, return the value of t representing 0.
    4. If t is the String type, return the empty String.
    5. If t is the Boolean type, return false.
    6. If t is the type named "undefined", return undefined.
    7. If t is the type named "null", return null.
    8. If t.[[Kind]] is union, then
      1. If t.[[Members]] contains the type named "null", return null.
      2. If t.[[Members]] contains the type named "undefined", return undefined.
      3. Return none.
    9. If t.[[Kind]] is array, then
      1. If t.[[Extent]] is dynamic, return a new empty array of the type t.
      2. If t.[[Extent]] is 0, return a new empty array of the type t.
      3. Let values be a new empty List.
      4. Repeat t.[[Extent]] times:
        1. Let d be DefaultValueOf(t.[[Element]]).
        2. If d is none, return none.
        3. Append d to values.
      5. Return a new array of the type t whose elements, in order, are values, with value-type copying as required by 1.11.4.
    10. If t.[[Kind]] is tuple, then
      1. If t has an established tuple sequence domain involving finite or nested rest expansion (1.14.1), then
        1. Let values be a new empty List.
        2. For each fixed position of that domain, with any unbounded run empty, in order, do
          1. Let d be the position's formed declared default if present, and DefaultValueOf(the position's type) otherwise.
          2. If d is none, return none.
          3. Append d to values.
        3. Return a new tuple of the type t whose elements, in order, are values, with value-type copying as required by 1.11.4 and its complete positional storage domain.
      2. Let values be a new empty List.
      3. For each element e of t.[[Elements]] whose [[Rest]] is false, in order, do
        1. Let d be none.
        2. If e.[[Initial]] is none, set d to DefaultValueOf(e.[[Type]]).
        3. Otherwise, set d to its [[Initial]] converted at the position's type by Table 23.
        4. If d is none, return none.
        5. Append d to values.
      4. Return a new tuple of the type t whose elements, in order, are values, with value-type copying as required by 1.11.4.
    11. If t.[[Kind]] is parameterized, then
      1. Let d be DefaultValueOf(t.[[Base]]).
      2. If d is none, return none.
      3. Let e be a new empty Object, which is the metadata of a value of t.[[Base]] that carries none.
      4. Let crossed be Completion(ConvertParameterization(d, e, t.[[Metadata]])).
      5. If crossed is an abrupt completion, return none.
      6. Return crossed.[[Value]].
    12. If t.[[Kind]] is literal, return t.[[Value]].
    13. If t.[[Kind]] is nominal and t denotes a value type class, return the instance of t each of whose fields, public and private, holds the default of the field's type as that type stands for t, or none if any field's type has no default.
    14. Return none.

    Default aggregates carry their declared element or positional backing contracts, including nested aggregates. Each needed default is computed once per position in order, without a separate availability probe; failure retains earlier independent computation effects but exposes no partially constructed aggregate.

    A ZERO extent is answered before the element is consulted. A fixed array's default is its extent filled with the element's default, so an element with none leaves the array with none — but at extent zero there is nothing to fill, and the element's default is not needed. Asking for it first would make [0].<never> have no default while [0].<uint8> has one, a difference no value of either can observe, both being the empty array and the same value the dynamic extent already takes. The step matters where an element type is reached through a type parameter rather than written, since a generic body is checked once for every instantiation and a declaration of [0].<_T_> must not become unwritable at the instantiations whose argument has no default.

    It is a type error to declare a binding or a field with a type t and no initializer when DefaultValueOf(t) is none.

    A PRIVATE field is filled like a public one. Its participation is the same as its participation in the layout — "private fields participate in the memory layout exactly as public fields do, which is why the value type rule counts both" — so a class whose only field is private has a default, and only the absence of a TYPE disqualifies a field, never the kind of its name.

    For a GENERIC class the field types are those of the APPLICATION, not of the declaration. G<4> whose field is declared [N].<uint8> has a field of type [4].<uint8>, so its default is a four-element zero-filled array; the declaration's own field type, whose extent is still the parameter, has no default and would otherwise leave every application of every such class without one.

    A parameterization's default is its base's zero having crossed into it, by the same conversion an initializer of the base's type crosses (6.3), so that let _x_: _T_; and let _x_: _T_ = 0; succeed together and fail together. Three consequences follow from the crossing rather than from a rule of its own. A meta type whose validate refuses the base's zero leaves the parameterization with no default, since the crossing throws and the step reports none: float64.<{ min: 1 }> has no zero because 0 is not one of its values. A brand for which no cast is declared has no default either, being "reachable only by construction" and a declaration without an initializer not being one. And a parameterization whose base declares a cast has the crossed zero, which is what keeps a unit type zero-fillable: Velocity is a float64 whose dimensions meta type defines no validate, so the cast admits the zero and let _v_: Velocity; holds 0 m/s.

    The meta types and casts declared in the surrounding realm are those declared as of the operation's application, as they are for the metadata subtype judgment and for the same reason: a parameterization may be written above the declarations that govern it, so the checking pass processes a source text's meta declarations and its primitive blocks' implicit cast operators before applying this operation (1.2.8), and whether a declaration needs an initializer is answered against those. Two call sites fix the realm rather than taking the current one, because in each the value is produced for a program that is not the one asking. An unwritten ThreadLocal read (41) takes the default in the realm in which the ThreadLocal was created, so that two agents reading one storage read one value. Reflect.defineProperty with a type and no value (1.12.6) takes it in the realm of the Type Object it was given, which is the only call site at which a program chooses the moment.

    Every default above is a zero, or, for a type with exactly one value, that value: the numeric zero, the empty String, false, null, the one value of a literal type, and an array or an aggregate whose storage is zero-filled. A literal type is the one case where a default is not chosen but forced — there is nothing to prefer a zero over, since no other value is of the type — and it is the reason the phrase is not simply "a zero". It takes nothing away from the fill below: a class holding a field of literal type has no layout at all, so no storage is described by it, and where a layout exists every default in it is a zero. Zero-filling is part of the semantics and not an optimization a program may opt out of, and no form of this proposal allocates without it. What is filled for an aggregate is its layout (9), padding included, so two instances of one value type class that are === field by field are also equal byte for byte.

    An aggregate has a default exactly where its parts do: a value type class where every field's type does, a fixed-extent array where its element's type does, and a tuple where every position it fills does. A parameterized field is the case to watch, since the step above gives a parameterization a default only where its base's zero can cross into it. A Vector3 of three Meter fields is zero-fillable exactly where float64 declares the cast into the dimensions meta type, and let _d_: [10].<Vector3>; is a type error where it does not — not because a unit has no zero, but because nothing in that program says how a bare zero becomes one. Writing that cast is what gives a design's unit types their zeros, and with it the aggregates holding them.

    Read the other way, the same rule is how a type says that no zero of it is meaningful. A class that needs its constructor to run states that by holding a field whose type has no default (1.11.2), and a brand into which no cast is declared is such a type: its values arrive only by construction, through the operators its base declares (6.5), so an aggregate holding one has no zero-filled form and says so at the declaration rather than at the first use.

    Note

    The reason is security rather than convenience. An allocation that exposed the bytes of a previously freed one would leak whatever had been there: another script's data, a former secret, or a heap pointer that defeats address space layout randomization. A fresh page from the operating system is already zero, so the fill costs nothing on a large new allocation, and reused memory must be cleared regardless, so there is nothing to gain by exposing it. The one pattern an uninitialized form would serve, allocate and then fill from input, is served by placement new over an existing buffer and by array views.

    A type with no default is one for which no zero is meaningful, and the operation reports that rather than inventing one. A union of two non-nullable types is the ordinary case: let x: uint8 | string; has two candidate zeros and no reason to prefer either, so it requires an initializer. symbol, object, a function type, and a class whose construction must run are the others.

    The design states the defaults for the numeric, SIMD, String, Boolean, nullable, and array types and does not reach the rest, so the boundaries above are supplied here and need review. Three deserve attention. A bigint is given the zero 0n on the same reasoning as the other numeric types. A tuple defaults element-wise, which follows from a tuple of value types being laid out contiguously, but a tuple with a defaulted trailing position already has an initializer for that position, which 1.14.10 reconciles. A value type class defaults field-wise, which is what makes let d: [10].<A>; hold ten zero-filled instances as the memory layout extension requires, but it means a class can be brought into existence without its constructor running, which 1.11.2 endorses.

    1.8.4 Typed Initializers

    A binding declared with a TypedInitializer takes the type of its initializer rather than the any type. Its declared type is the Static Type of the AssignmentExpression, and it is initialized to that expression's value.

    Note

    let a := new MyType(); declares a of type MyType, where let a = new MyType(); would declare it of the any type. The two spellings differ in what may be assigned afterwards, not in what is stored: the first rejects a = 5, the second permits it. := therefore removes the redundancy of let a: MyType = new MyType(); without introducing inference anywhere the program did not ask for it, which is why it is a distinct operator rather than a rule that an initialized binding infers its type. An unannotated binding remaining any is what keeps an untyped program untyped.

    It is a type error if the Static Type of the initializer is the any type, since let a := f(); where f is untyped would declare a binding of the any type through a syntax that asks for a type.

    1.8.5 Narrowing

    A test that establishes something about a value's type refines the Static Type of that value in the branch the test guards. The Static Type of a reference to a binding at a given point is its declared type refined by the narrowing facts that hold there.

    The narrowing facts that hold at a point are the join of the facts on every path of control reaching it. A path through a statement that cannot complete normally (25) contributes none, and where several paths reach a point the Static Type of a path there is the union of its Static Types on those paths, a path no fact narrows contributing its type before the test. So the statements after an if statement one of whose branches cannot complete normally see the facts of the other branch, as its else would; the exit of a loop sees the facts of its test's failure joined with those at each break that leaves it, after the loop rule below has discarded what its body can reassign; the end of a switch with no default sees the facts of each clause that completes joined with those of the fall-out past its last label; and a catch or finally block sees the facts at the try statement's entry less those about a path the try block can assign. Where a test is a conjunction, the facts of its truth are those of every operand, each operand's facts holding where the next is evaluated; where it is a disjunction, the facts of its falsity are those of every operand; a false conjunction and a true disjunction establish none of their operands' facts.

    Narrowing preserves whether the binding participates in typed operand judgments. Use the original declaration's contract for participation and the current narrowed Static Type for the judgment itself. Thus a typed nullable binding narrowed to null cannot support an ordinary property operation, and a typed union narrowed to a Symbol cannot support numeric conversion. A narrowing fact introduces no lexical declaration or annotation: genuine shadowing, explicit any and mutation invalidation retain their ordinary effects.

    v above is a reference to a binding or a chain of property accesses over one, a path, and s is its Static Type where the test occurs. A path names the SAME PLACE however often it is evaluated, which bounds what may be one: a chain of plain names from a binding or this, private names included; an object property access whose computed key is an established constant String, including an immutable binding naming that String; and an index into a FIXED-extent array whose index cannot change - a literal, or a binding the source never assigns. A call anywhere in the chain is not a path, since two evaluations of h.get().p are two values; nor is an index into an array whose extent can change; nor an optional link a?.b, which names a different place depending on whether its base is nullish. A computed key must require no unknown evaluation or coercion to establish its identity. Key identity is property identity: v["tag"] and v.tag name the same property, while v["a.b"] and v.a.b name different places. Parentheses around a test or its operands preserve recognition, including (typeof v) === "number"; this does not make an effectful comma expression transparent. An expression that is not a path narrows nothing rather than narrowing unsoundly; its test is still a narrowing form, and where it decides a branch 1.8.5.4 judges it with s the Static Type of the expression. A narrowing fact holds in any position the test governs, not only in the body of an if: the two branches of a conditional expression are narrowed by its condition, the right operand of && is narrowed by the truth of its left operand, and the right operand of || by the falsity of its left. A test decides a branch in the test of an if, while, do-while or for, in the condition of a conditional expression, in the left operand of &&, || and ??, whose right operand it decides, in the Expression of a MatchGuard, which decides whether the arm runs once the pattern has matched and whose facts hold in the arm, in a case label of a switch whose captured discriminant has an established singleton Boolean value (below), and in the positions nested in any of these that decide the same branch: the right operand of && or ||, the last operand of a comma expression, and each arm of a conditional expression. The right operand of && or || that is not itself in such a position decides no branch, since its value is the result. A fact about a path holds until the path or a prefix of it is assigned a value whose type is not within the narrowed type. == and != narrow as === and !== do wherever the Static Types of both operands make the two agree, which a union of literal types over one base always does, so the design's this.country == 'US' narrows and a comparison that could coerce does not.

    The constant key in an in test may be supplied by an established singleton String operand, including a constant alias, rather than only by literal syntax. Resolve the key without executing evaluation or coercion, then apply the existing per-member typed-storage presence judgment. A broad or multiple-key domain and a structural property annotation alone establish no guaranteed presence. Parentheses around an instanceof constructor preserve its identity; an immutable constructor alias may supply the same nominal implication when its captured constructor and the applicable instance-check semantics are established. A callable signature, unknown constructor selection, or custom or replaced Symbol.hasInstance operation supplies no nominal implication by this rule.

    An operand e names a literal type L where it is a literal expression — a numeric literal, optionally preceded by - or +, a String, BigInt or Boolean literal, or a NoSubstitutionTemplate, which is the String literal it spells — and L is its literal type; where it is a reference to a const binding with no type annotation whose initializer is such an expression, and L is that expression's literal type; where it is void applied to such an expression, and L is undefined; or where it is an enumerator reference E.A, and L is the literal type of the enumerator's value over the enum, so that two enumerators of one enum are disjoint exactly where their values differ and names sharing one value are one type (1.11.8). No other operand names one: an expression whose value merely folds to a constant does not, so which comparisons narrow is visible in the source.

    Where a switch's captured discriminant has an established singleton Boolean value, from a Boolean literal, an operand naming that literal type, or its current narrowed Static Type, each case label is a test deciding whether its clause is entered, read as the label's own test for the captured value true and as its negation for false. A discriminant whose type admits both Boolean values supplies neither proof. Evaluate and capture the discriminant once; label effects do not change the captured value. Its facts hold in the statements it reaches unless an earlier clause can fall into them, and the labels after it, which are tested only where it failed, see its negation, as the default does where no clause falls into it.

    The types whose typeof is "object" include every array and tuple type, the type of a typed class, and every vector, complex, rational and composite type, besides null; the types whose typeof is "function" include every function type. An object type is not among the types whose typeof is either, since a function with the required properties is a value of it; nor is an untyped class, whose constructor may return a function, nor the type of a global constructor, whose values are its instances by prototype chain, which a function can be given. A typeof test of a value of one of those can go either way.

    Note 1

    The bare-v row uses the existing representable truthy and falsy parts. A boolean becomes true or false; boolean | null becomes true or false | null. Falsity is not evidence of absence alone: zero and the empty String also reach the false edge. Where their precise subsets are not represented, numeric, String and BigInt members conservatively contribute to both parts. The literal-idiom exceptions and ordinary write invalidation still apply.

     Note 2

    Facts reach paths because the types this proposal narrows are about fields as much as bindings, and if (addr.country == 'US') is the design's own example. Assignment to a prefix discards a fact about everything under it, which is the design's account of a mode reassigned after a name was narrowed by it. A LOOP discards a fact about every name its body can reassign, before the body is entered: a body is reasoned about once, and a read that precedes the assignment textually still follows it on the next pass, so a fact that the body invalidates cannot be held for any part of it. A CALL discards a fact about any name some function body assigns to. A call can reach a binding the caller narrowed - a closure over it needs only to be in scope - and the caller cannot see which one, so the conservative fact is whether any function assigns that name at all. A name no function assigns is untouched, which is what keeps an ordinary call from discarding anything. The boundary check remains the backstop for what static reasoning cannot reach at all, such as a value arriving through any (Table 23).

    1.8.5.1 Propagation of Narrowing Facts

    The type errors this clause states, among them an excluded value that leaves nothing, a repeated test and a loop that can never be entered, apply only in checked code (1.2.5). Outside checked code the same facts are established without error.

    Narrowing is a bounded analysis of the control flow of the source text. A fact identifies a lexical binding and, where applicable, a path rooted in that binding; equal spellings in different scopes do not identify the same binding. A fact does not change the declared type of a store, the declaration's participation in typed operand judgments, or the validity of a reference under 2.10.

    Keep separate environments of facts for the true and false results of a test, and for normal, return, throw, break and continue completions. A break or continue completion identifies its target statement. Sequential evaluation passes only normal completions to the next position. At an alternative join, retain a fact only if every incoming completion supplies it, joining its possible types with CanonicalizeType of their union. A predecessor with no fact is unknown, not unreachable. An established impossible true or false result contributes no predecessor to that result join; keep result feasibility separate from the facts on a reachable result. Established truthiness may exclude an opposite result without making a literal idiom an error. Unreachable source retains its ordinary syntax and type checks but supplies no outgoing completion. Leaving a lexical scope removes its local bindings and retains facts about surviving bindings. Checking a nested function does not execute it or export its completion facts to the enclosing evaluation.

    The following transfers apply to the narrowing forms in Table 24, including declared predicates and resolved metadata narrowings. They also apply when computing a conditional arm's Static Type, rather than only when diagnosing a test.

    • Parentheses preserve both result environments and built-in logical negation exchanges them. A declared logical-not operator uses its selected result contract instead; it need not negate the receiver's truthiness. For a && b, evaluate b under the true environment of a; the true result is the true environment of b, and the false result joins the false environment of a with that of b. For a || b, exchange true and false in this rule. Process effects in evaluation order, so an operand can invalidate a fact established by an earlier operand.
    • A comma expression evaluates its operands in order and takes both result environments from its last operand. A conditional expression evaluates its condition, evaluates each arm under the corresponding condition environment, and separately joins the arms' true results and their false results. An if statement joins only the normal completions of its arms; an omitted arm supplies its incoming environment.
    • The right operand of ?? and ??= is governed by the left operand's nullish environment. The right operands of &&= and ||= are governed by the same environments as their non-assignment forms. An optional chain evaluates its computed keys and arguments under the present environment of the receiver at that optional link, and joins its normal result with its skipped paths. Effects in an earlier key or argument may invalidate facts before a later one. A captured callee value does not establish that its binding still holds that value. A logical assignment checks its store against the declared destination type and invalidates affected facts when that store occurs.
    • A while or for test's true environment enters its body. A for update joins the body's normal completions and the continues targeting that loop. A do-while test has the same incoming completions from its body. Returns, throws and breaks do not enter those positions. The normal successor of a loop joins the false test completion, where present, with the breaks targeting that loop. An inner loop or switch's break is not an exit from an outer loop. A for-in, for-of or for-await-of loop also admits the path on which iteration ends without entering its body.
    • Apply loop widening before reasoning about the repeated positions: discard incoming facts about bindings the loop can write and, where it contains a call, bindings subject to captured writes or other call effects under 1.6.2.12. The loop's own tests can establish new facts. This rule requires neither a fixed point over iterations nor a proof of termination. An omitted for test or a literal true loop test supplies no false exit.
    • Switch label selection and clause execution are separate flows. Evaluate labels in their selection order, passing failed comparisons to the next label. The default's selection environment follows every failed label, including labels textually after the default. A clause body joins its selected entry with normal fallthrough from the preceding body. Case-block lexical declarations retain their ordinary shared scope and temporal dead zone; an unrelated declaration does not disable a discriminant fact. A typeof switch refines the original operand, retaining every type with the selected tag. A singleton Boolean switch uses the label's corresponding result environment. A singleton Boolean label can likewise select the corresponding result environment of a captured Boolean discriminant, including an original numeric predicate, an admitted Object.is test, or a preserved predicate alias. Capture that result once and apply subsequent label effects to its source relations before selection. A label that changes the discriminant binding cannot refine its new value from a comparison with the captured discriminant. Switch exits join normal fallthrough, breaks targeting the switch, and any unmatched path admitted by its existing exhaustiveness rules.
    • A labelled statement consumes only breaks naming that label. A try statement joins normal completion of its body with normal completion of its handlers. Handler entry conservatively admits exceptions from expressions and cleanup, widening facts that the try body may invalidate; a typed catch binding keeps its declared filter as its store type and receives the residual entry fact specified in 1.7.8. A finally block is checked under the join of the incoming completion environments, including possible implicit exceptions. Its normal completion preserves each incoming completion's kind and target, carrying forward facts it did not invalidate and applying the facts its normal completion establishes. An abrupt finalizer completion replaces the incoming completion. A finalizer write or call can therefore invalidate a fact on a pending break, continue or return.
    • A match subject that is a stable place retains its lexical binding identity through parentheses and property paths. A selected clause receives MatchNarrow of the remaining captured subject type and its pattern, including a scalar literal subset of a broader primitive type. Apply the existing numeric literal adoption rules before constructing that subset; do not choose an arbitrary numeric domain. An unrepresentable Type Record complement remains conservative; retain the internal scalar exclusions specified below. Publish a captured-subject fact about the current place only while the place and its prefixes still denote that captured subject. For ordinary match, the next clause joins the pattern-miss environment with the matched-pattern, guard-false environment. An irrefutable pattern supplies no miss predecessor. The arm receives the guard-true environment. Project away clause-local bindings at each exit, and process pattern and guard effects before joining. Alternative arm bodies do not execute one another; join their normal completions at the result. The existing match-all selection and exhaustiveness rules remain separate.
    • When an ordinary do expression supplies a test result, associate the true and false environments with each normal completion value producer identified by 37.2, including values carried by UpdateEmpty and breaks consumed within the expression. Its producers are deciding positions to the extent the enclosing result decides a branch. Separately join environments for truthy and falsy normal results; a completion with no value contributes the undefined result. Apply effects occurring after a producer to the facts attached to its captured result, including effects of a normally completing finally block. An abrupt completion escaping the expression contributes no result environment. Remove local bindings when leaving their scopes. Unknown completion sources remain conservative. The generator forms of do expressions do not use this transfer.
    • For a tested coalescing expression, distinguish operand selection from result truthiness. Partition the captured present-left value by its truthy and falsy parts, publishing those parts to its preserved origin; a Boolean present value therefore separates into true and false. Join the truthy results of the present-left path and the nullish-right path for its true environment, and the falsy results of those paths for its false environment. An alternative with established opposite truthiness contributes no predecessor to that result. Apply right-operand effects before propagating its result facts. Bare-place tests use the truthy and falsy parts in Table 24.
    • A built-in strict equality or inequality comparison between a Boolean-valued expression and an established singleton Boolean value composes the expression's result environments, exchanging them for equality with false or inequality with true. Either operand order is admitted. Evaluate both operands once in source order, applying later effects before exporting facts about an earlier captured result. Unknown comparison values, coercing comparisons, and user-defined operations do not establish this correspondence.
    • When an assignment expression supplies a test result, propagate the established result producer's true and false environments through destination evaluation, conversions, and store effects in their specified order. Partition the actual normal result by ToBoolean, including a non-Boolean result. An established identity-preserving assignment result carries the captured right operand's truth environments through the store. A fact about the current source survives only if destination evaluation, conversion and store effects preserve that source identity and the established result correspondence. A setter can replace the source while the assignment still returns the captured right operand; do not reread the destination or source to obtain that result. For logical assignment, separately join skipped and stored alternatives by the truth of the resulting value; a skipped alternative supplies no fact established only by its right operand. Check the declared destination type as usual. This transfer concerns the tested expression's result, not an unconditional fact about its destination at later reads. An unresolved store, accessor, conversion, or selected operation supplies no unsupported preservation proof.
    • When an optional chain supplies a test result, each skipped nullish alternative contributes its undefined result only to the false environment. Separately join the true and false results of evaluated alternatives, including a selected predicate's argument facts under the declared-call rules. This transfer does not infer a predicate contract for an untyped callee binding. The false environment may include a present receiver producing a falsy value. Refine a stable receiver or argument place only while it still denotes its captured value after key, argument, getter, and call effects; the optional expression itself does not become a path.
    • Strict comparison and switch selection can also consume an optional result's alternatives. A skipped link contributes undefined; an equal-result selection excluding undefined, or an unequal-result selection against undefined, excludes that skipped alternative. Preserve the evaluated alternatives' receiver-presence facts only while the captured places survive all subsequent operand and label effects. A repeated accessor read need not reproduce its captured value; an open structural property contract alone supplies no such preservation proof. o?.tag === "a" can therefore establish presence, but o?.tag !== "a" and o?.tag === undefined do not generally establish it. Evaluate each receiver, key, getter, argument and label once. Switch body entry still joins selection with fallthrough. These alternatives may be transformed by the established typeof tag mapping before selection: a skipped link contributes the String "undefined", and a present result contributes its established tags. Selecting a tag other than "undefined" excludes every skipped alternative; selecting "undefined" need not prove absence, since a present result may be undefined. This is a relation to the evaluated optional result, not permission to repeat a getter or reevaluate its receiver.
    • For switch selection from an optional result, carry its remaining evaluated and skipped alternatives from each failed comparison to the next label. If a label has an established singleton value, remove from the failed-selection alternatives every established singleton result that compares equal to it by the admitted built-in strict equality, retaining every other possible result. Strict equality identifies the two signs of zero within the same numeric type and never matches NaN; mathematical equality across unrelated numeric types is not a proof of selection. Apply the existing literal-adoption rules when establishing the operands' value domains. A broad primitive domain is not exhausted by removing one of its values. A non-singleton label supplies no whole-domain exclusion merely because its type admits the discriminant's type. When no evaluated result remains, remove the evaluated alternative; when the skipped result is excluded, remove the skipped alternative. Later labels and the default receive only the remaining alternatives, after their reached label effects. Join selected entry with normal fallthrough before checking a clause body. A present result of undefined and the skipped undefined result remain distinct alternatives with different receiver facts, even though one label can select both. Apply the same rule to typeof-transformed optional results using their String tag values.
    • For built-in strict equality between two known primitive domains, retain on the equal edge each operand's members that admit an equal value from the other's captured domain. Numeric compatibility follows strict value identity and the existing literal-adoption rules, not mathematical equality across unrelated numeric types or a nominal type intersection. Capture each operand at its evaluation point; later writes, getters and calls can prevent projecting a captured domain onto its current place. Projection requires an established data value; a binding or proved data slot can supply this identity, but an open structural property contract alone cannot rule out a varying accessor result. Apply the same equal-edge transfer to an ordinary non-singleton switch label, using the captured discriminant and the value produced by evaluating that label. Selection is joined with incoming fallthrough before checking the body. The unequal edge supplies no whole-domain exclusion in general. Unknown domains, unresolved metadata and coercing operations supply no such proof. Existing operator-admission rules remain in force.
    • When an ordinary match supplies a test result, separately join its selected arms' normal true and false results after pattern and guard effects. Block arms use the completion-value producer rules of an ordinary do expression, including UpdateEmpty and effects after a captured producer. Escaping abrupt completions contribute no result, and arm-local bindings are removed at the exit. The collection returned by match all does not use this scalar transfer.
    • When a pipeline supplies a test result, its body supplies the result environments under its own topic binding. Remove that binding at the pipeline exit and retain facts about surviving outer bindings. A topic may additionally carry the identity of its input stable place: publish a topic fact about that place only where the place and its prefixes still denote the captured input value and the existing membership-stability rules admit the fact. Calls and other non-path inputs supply no source-place identity. Nested topics have distinct identities. The topic remains a value binding; this transfer permits neither a reference to it nor an extension of reference liveness.
    • Entry to a for-in iteration establishes that its captured enumeration source is neither null nor undefined. Publish this fact about the current source place only while its identity survives loop widening, enumeration effects, iteration-target assignment, and lexical shadowing. A source that can change between iterations cannot be narrowed anew from its old captured value. In particular, enumeration callbacks may replace an aliased property or reference source; mere syntactic absence of an assignment to its spelling is not an identity proof. The successor still joins the zero-iteration path. The for-of and for-await-of protocols establish no such fact by this rule.

    Parentheses around a switch discriminant preserve its selection rules and facts. A constant range label that admits no value of the captured discriminant's established numeric domain is an impossible test under 1.8.5.4. Range selection uses the member-wise MatchNarrow and MissNarrow rules of 24.3 for the current place while that place still denotes the captured subject. Keep the union of preceding proved constant intervals in selection order: a later range label is an impossible selection where none of its values in the captured numeric domain remain outside that union. Use exact established endpoints and domains, respecting open and closed endpoints and integer adjacency; unknown bounds contribute no coverage proof. Partial overlap alone is not impossibility. Clause execution still joins selected entry with fallthrough, so redundant selection does not make all statements beneath that label unreachable. These rules add neither range-based default rejection nor range coverage to switch exhaustiveness.

    The result producers in these tested-expression transfers are deciding positions for the impossible-test judgment to the extent that their results decide the enclosing branch. The transfers export facts about surviving bindings, not new lexical bindings from a pattern, match arm, completion block, or topic scope. They do not by themselves extend a pattern binding's governed scope. A producer used only as a value remains subject to the existing non-deciding-query rules.

    A store may retain an existing fact about its target if the established stored result, after any required conversion, is a subtype of that fact. Check the store against the declared destination type, process source effects in evaluation order, and invalidate affected descendant paths. Retaining a property fact also requires that evaluation has not replaced a prefix of the captured destination. An unresolved result or conversion supplies no preservation proof. A successful participating initialization or simple store also establishes a new current-value fact where its post-conversion domain is proved. Complete dependent store facts under 1.6.2.12. Capture that result at its production point and apply destination, conversion and store effects before publishing it. For logical assignment, join the skipped and stored alternatives. The declared destination remains the store contract, including its callable, predicate and contextual-void contracts; do not replace it with a raw initializer signature. Ordinary untyped bindings do not acquire a contract by this rule. Unknown conversion results, accessor stores, or changed destination origins supply no new fact. Reference liveness is unchanged.

    An immutable Boolean binding initialized from a recognized test retains that producer's established true and false implications under the following source-identity rules. Capture each implication's lexical subject and value identity at initialization; a later test of the Boolean replays an implication only while its subject still denotes that captured value. The Boolean's value is not reevaluated, and it grants no reference or lifetime. A mutable Boolean, a shadowing binding, a relevant write, an uncertain alias effect, or an invalid reference origin supplies no such replay. Preserve these identities through branch joins and loop widening; no fact may survive an unconstrained incoming predecessor.

    An initializer that reads a preserved immutable Boolean alias consumes that alias's result environments under these same rules. A copy, negation or other recognized composition therefore retains implications about the original source places, not only the immediate Boolean operand. Each source identity includes its declaring binding and captured value; a matching name in another lexical environment supplies no implication. Apply all initializer effects before retaining a relation, and do not recover a source relation already invalidated before the copy. Retain only the source implications established by the selected result: unrelated facts in the initializer's incoming environment do not become properties of the Boolean.
